title: ～きり — only ～; ever since ～
summary: Has two uses: after a noun or quantity it means 'only,' and after a past-form verb it means 'since that one time, nothing further happened.' A negative statement often follows.

body.p: 会ったきり and 出かけたきり mean that action was the last one, with no later development. A negative or worrying statement often follows: 出かけたきり帰ってこない.
In 二人きり or それっきり it means 'only' or 'nothing more.' Compared with だけ, it carries a feeling of regret or specialness. 一度きり works the same way.

examples.ja: 彼（かれ）とは一度（いちど）会（あ）ったきりです。
examples.romaji: Kare to wa ichido atta kiri desu.

examples.ja: 祖父（そふ）は朝（あさ）出（で）かけたきり、まだ帰（かえ）ってこない。
examples.romaji: Sofu wa asa dekaketa kiri, mada kaette konai.
examples.tr: My grandfather went out in the morning and still hasn't come back.

examples.ja: 大事（だいじ）な話（はなし）があるので、二人（ふたり）きりで会（あ）いたい。
examples.romaji: Daiji na hanashi ga aru node, futarikiri de aitai.
examples.tr: I have something important to discuss, so I want to meet just the two of us.

pitfalls: With verbs it follows the past form; 行くきり is wrong.
After verb + きり a negative statement usually follows. 出かけたきり、元気だ is awkward.
